quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns drivers that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle, like a motorcycle, is going or how far away it is. Do not assume other drivers will see you clearly or judge your speed correctly.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of your lane where another driver can see you as soon as possible.
Stop at the sign or signal, then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of your lane where another driver can see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself so other drivers can see you as early as possible.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should stay at least ________ behind the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists should stay at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. In bad conditions, increase this distance.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, you should:

options.text: Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead is slippery when wet.

questions.question: In general, what is the best position to ride in within a lane?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. A good rider changes position as conditions change.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: One danger of riding next to another vehicle is that:

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can see you easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could move into your lane or block your escape route if you need to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the formation you should use:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, entering or leaving highways.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT important for helmet protection?
questions.explanation: A helmet protects best when it meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly around your head, and has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When you need to react to a road hazard, you should NOT:

options.text: Stay silent and ignore other drivers.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to alert others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay silent and ignore other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers you are there by using your horn, lights, and signals. Slow down or speed up as needed for the situation. Change your lane position or direction if necessary.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Always brake and swerve separately. Never brake while swerving because your motorcycle may fall over.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a rider should NOT:

options.text: Position the motorcycle so other drivers can see it clearly.
Ready the clutch and brakes to react faster.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you. Have your clutch and both brakes ready so you can react quickly. Slow down as you approach. Do not change speed or position suddenly, as other drivers may misunderstand your actions.

questions.question: Eye protection is:
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear eye protection on a moving motorcycle. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You must release the rear brake immediately.

questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually maintain control as long as the motorcycle stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, secure it:
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure to avoid throwing off your motorcycle's balance.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop behind it on the road.
Wait until it starts moving again.
Move to a different lane away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from it.
questions.explanation: When you approach an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside help with flashing lights, change lanes to give it more space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight hours. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times, even during the day.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you?

options.text: It gives you more time to respond to hazards.
It stops you from finding an escape route.
It gives you space to maneuver your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops you from finding an escape route.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and the vehicle ahead gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. This space also lets you safely steer your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding with a group of motorcyclists, a staggered formation:

options.text: Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.
Should be used when riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is generally good, but groups should switch to single-file formation when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, a rider should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Turn by using only the handle bars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before you enter the turn.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Look over their shoulder when turning or going into a curve.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when turning or going into a curve.
questions.explanation: Before the passenger gets on, ask them to look over your shoulder in the direction of any turn or curve. This helps both you and the bike lean the right way.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Provide you with an escape route.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.explanation: Good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should keep other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if a hazard appears.
